toolchain.apca: PASS (72/72) — script fixed to point at design-core tokens.css (F-D9 resolved)
toolchain.note: pnpm audit:apca npm script itself is misconfigured (F-D9); run the script directly against tokens.css.

findings.title: P31 theme tokens never load at runtime — app renders on browser defaults
findings.detail: main.tsx imports only '@p31ca/design-core/css/all.css', 'container.css', and './index.css'. The built CSS defines exactly 3 --p31-* custom properties (--p31-container-font/padding/gap). Every var(--p31-*) reference in index.css and CatalogPage.css therefore resolves to its fallback (Canvas, CanvasText, currentColor, or a hardcoded hex/oklch). The portal renders with browser-default colors and fonts, not the P31 rebel theme.
findings.evidence: Computed by scanning dist/assets/index-D1xDgZfs.css: 3 --p31-* definitions total; theme-p31ca.css and tokens.css are exported by design-core but not imported.
findings.recommendation: Import '@p31ca/design-core/css/tokens.css' and 'theme-p31ca.css' (or the combined 'index.css') before './index.css', and set data-brand="p31ca" / data-theme="rebel" on <html>.

findings.title: Duplicate Enter-to-send handlers — Ctrl+Enter double-submits
findings.detail: A global window keydown listener fires handleSend on Ctrl/Cmd+Enter; the textarea also has an inline onKeyDown that fires handleSend on Enter when !shiftKey. When focus is in the textarea and the user presses Ctrl+Enter, BOTH handlers run: the inline handler matches (Enter, !shiftKey) and the global handler matches (ctrlKey+Enter). handleSend reads `input`, calls setInput(''), then handleClarify(text) — the second invocation re-reads the stale `input` closure and can enqueue the same prompt twice, producing duplicate user messages and double generation.
findings.evidence: SandboxChat.tsx:482-487 (global) and :650-655 (inline) both call handleSend; no guard prevents the second call in the same keypress.
findings.recommendation: Consolidate submission into one handler: have the inline textarea onKeyDown delegate to a single submit path and remove the duplicate branch, or gate the global handler with `if (e.target === textareaRef.current) return;`.

findings.title: CatalogDetail Place affordability uses a hardcoded threshold, not live spoons
findings.detail: canAfford is computed as `entry.spoonCost <= 3`, ignoring the real useSpoons() value. A component with spoonCost 4-5 is permanently disabled even at spoons 5; a component with spoonCost <= 3 is enabled even at spoons 0, and the Place click then silently fails because placeComponent() returns { success:false }. The gamification store already enforces the correct check.
findings.evidence: CatalogDetail.tsx:47 hardcodes the threshold; gamification.ts:42-51 compares against useSpoons.getState().spoons.
findings.recommendation: Read spoons from useSpoons inside CatalogDetail and set `canAfford = spoons >= entry.spoonCost`, or pass the affordability flag from the parent.

findings.title: Composer textarea disabled without aria-busy / aria-disabled on the input
findings.detail: The textarea is set to `disabled={generationStatus !== 'idle' || pendingClarify !== null}`. The composer contract requires `aria-busy when streaming`, and the disabled input is not announced as busy/disabled to assistive tech. The status indicator also lacks role/live region (see F-F3).
findings.evidence: SandboxChat.tsx:656 disables the textarea; contract required_aria lists 'aria-busy when streaming' and 'aria-live on status'.
findings.recommendation: Add aria-busy={generating} to the textarea (and aria-disabled when disabled) and role="status" + aria-live="polite" to the generation-status element.

findings.title: Generation status has no role="status" / aria-live
findings.detail: The 'Calling generator…' / 'Streaming…' status div has no role="status" or aria-live, so screen readers never announce generation state. Contract chat-composer requires `aria-live on status`.
findings.evidence: SandboxChat.tsx:616-621 renders .chat-generation-status with no live-region semantics.
findings.recommendation: Add role="status" aria-live="polite" to the status div.

findings.title: AgentSelector popover has no keyboard navigation or Escape close
findings.detail: The selector is a Button + role="menu" popover. It closes on outside mousedown only. No ArrowUp/Down movement, no Escape-to-close, no focus management, no typeahead. Keyboard users cannot operate the menu.
findings.evidence: AgentSelector.tsx:29-36 (outside click only), :40 (aria-expanded), :45 (role=menu); no onKeyDown handlers.
findings.recommendation: Add ArrowUp/Down navigation over role=menuitem options, Escape to close, and focus the active item on open.

findings.title: ClarifyGate options are not a radiogroup; no keyboard nav; contradictory label
findings.detail: Each option is a standalone aria-pressed button, not a role=radiogroup, so arrow-key selection is impossible. There is no fieldset/legend grouping. The submit button label 'Let defaults decide' is shown when answerCount===0 but the button is disabled until allAnswered (0===length only when there are no questions), so that label is effectively unreachable.
findings.evidence: ClarifyGate.tsx:43-55 (aria-pressed buttons), :62-67 (disabled submit + conditional label).
findings.recommendation: Use a radiogroup (role=radiogroup + role=radio, arrow-key selection) per question, or native inputs; fix the disabled/label logic so 'Let defaults decide' is actionable when the user wants defaults.

findings.title: Artifact code textarea has no aria-label; tabs use aria-pressed, not the tab pattern
findings.detail: The code-editor textarea has no aria-label (its visible text is the code). The preview/code/diff/inspect tabs use aria-pressed buttons instead of the tablist/tab pattern, so the artifact-pane contract's 'aria-label on tabs' requirement is unmet.
findings.evidence: ArtifactPane.tsx:487-498 (textarea, no aria-label); :398-410 (aria-pressed tabs).
findings.recommendation: Add aria-label="Code editor" to the textarea; convert tabs to role=tablist/tab with aria-selected and keyboard arrow navigation.

findings.title: Suggestion chip nests a real <button> inside a role="button" container
findings.detail: The chip is a div with role="button" tabIndex=0 and an onClick, but also contains a real dismiss <button> child. Nested interactive roles are an accessibility anti-pattern and can confuse screen-reader navigation.
findings.evidence: SandboxChat.tsx:623 (role=button on the container) and :625 (nested dismiss <button>).
findings.recommendation: Make the chip itself a real <button>, with the dismiss control a sibling (or a single button that opens an explicit dismiss action), removing the nested interactive.

findings.title: Catalog search is a <form> that never submits
findings.detail: The search is wrapped in a <form onSubmit={e => e.preventDefault()}> with no submit button and no Enter handling. The form element adds no value and signals a submit affordance that does not exist.
findings.evidence: CatalogPage.tsx:117-126.
findings.recommendation: Replace the <form> with a plain <div> or label wrapper, or implement a genuine submit/filter action.

findings.title: Split-pane handle is a focusable separator but has no value semantics
findings.detail: The resize handle has role="separator" aria-orientation="vertical" tabIndex=0 but no aria-valuemin/max/now, and no arrow-key resize handler. Keyboard users can focus it but cannot resize.
findings.evidence: SandboxPage.tsx:151-153.
findings.recommendation: Add aria-valuenow/valuemin/valuemax and ArrowLeft/Right handlers, or make it a non-focusable visual handle.

findings.title: Composer uses role="form" on a div, not a real <form>
findings.detail: The composer is a div with role="form" aria-label="Chat composer". A real <form> element (or a more specific role) would be more semantically correct and give native Enter/submit behavior.
findings.evidence: SandboxChat.tsx:615.
findings.recommendation: Use a real <form> element with the aria-label, and handle submit via onSubmit rather than keydown listeners.

findings.title: Six --p31-* tokens referenced in src are undeclared in any design-core CSS
findings.detail: These tokens are used but not declared in any design-core css file: --p31-accent-warm (CatalogPage.css), --p31-border-soft (CatalogPage.css), --p31-on-status (index.css:2036,2041), --p31-status-warn (index.css), --p31-surface-raised (CatalogPage.css), --p31-text-disabled (CatalogPage.css). Each resolves to its fallback.
findings.evidence: Cross-referenced the full declared-token set across P31-local-workspace/packages/design-core/src/css/*.css against all var(--p31-*) references in portals/chat/src.
findings.recommendation: Either add these tokens to the design-core token set, or replace them with declared equivalents (e.g. --p31-text-secondary for --p31-text-disabled, --p31-glass-border for --p31-border-soft).

findings.title: Hardcoded hex / rgba / oklch colors and inline styles in app source
findings.detail: The portal's own pipeline forbids hex, raw rgb()/rgba(), and inline styles, yet app source uses them: PreviewRenderer.tsx:137 has inline style with #0a0a0f (plus 13 inline styles total); ArtifactPane.tsx:50/72 use inline oklch outline + wrapFragment defaults; CatalogPage.css contains 22 hex and 26 rgba literals (e.g. #6C63FF, #00F0FF, rgba(0,0,0,...)); SpatialHover and ElementInspector use inline style; index.html has two inline-style elements. design-spec.html in public/ is a heavy contributor (12 hex, 26 rgba, 12 emoji) to the repo slop score.
findings.evidence: scripts/slop-eval.mjs --dir src reports: PreviewRenderer hardcoded_hex x1 + inline_style x13, SpatialHover inline_style x1, CatalogPage.css hardcoded_hex x22 + hardcoded_rgba x26, pipeline.ts hardcoded_rgba x2, missing_aria_icon x1.
findings.recommendation: Replace hex/rgba literals with declared tokens (or add the tokens), and move inline styles into index.css classes.

findings.title: html data-brand="willow" matches no design-core theme; theme-color hardcoded
findings.detail: <html data-brand="willow">. design-core themes key on data-brand="p31ca" / data-theme="rebel" (theme-p31ca.css) and others. 'willow' activates none of them, compounding F-D1. The meta theme-color is hardcoded to #818CF8 instead of a token.
findings.evidence: index.html:2 (data-brand=willow), :6 (theme-color #818CF8); theme-p31ca.css targets [data-brand='p31ca'] / [data-theme='rebel'].
findings.recommendation: Set data-brand="p31ca" and data-theme="rebel" (matching the portal brand 'Sandbox' app), and drive theme-color from a token.

findings.title: Non-token custom properties in CatalogPage.css
findings.detail: Uses --space-3, --radius-md, --radius-sm, --font which are not part of the design-core token set (declared names are --p31-space-*, --p31-radius-*). These resolve to nothing and fall through to the property default.
findings.evidence: CatalogPage.css:124 (var(--space-3)), :135/:248/:654 (var(--radius-md)), :138 (var(--font)), :684 (var(--radius-sm)).
findings.recommendation: Replace with --p31-space-*, --p31-radius-*, --p31-font-sans.

findings.title: Typography drift: system-ui instead of Plus Jakarta Sans canon
findings.detail: The design rubric specifies 'Plus Jakarta Sans, not system-ui'. index.css sets font-family to var(--p31-font-sans, system-ui) and the composer input uses the same fallback. Combined with F-D1 (tokens never load), rendered type is system-ui, not the canon font.
findings.evidence: src/index.css:1-2; specs/README.md rubric row 'Typography | Plus Jakarta Sans, not system-ui'.
findings.recommendation: After wiring tokens (F-D1), ensure --p31-font-sans resolves to Plus Jakarta Sans and that the font file is loaded.

findings.title: slop score at regression threshold on full-repo scan
findings.detail: src-only slop is 17 (acceptable, delta -2 vs baseline 19). Full-repo scan (including public/design-spec.html and index.html) is 22 — exactly at the threshold 22 (acceptable-elevated, delta +3). design-spec.html contributes 12 hex, 26 rgba, 12 emoji, 58 glass matches.
findings.evidence: node scripts/slop-eval.mjs --dir . : score 22, baseline {score:19, threshold:22}, verdict acceptable-elevated. --dir src: score 17.
findings.recommendation: Move design-spec.html out of the scanned surface (or tokenize it), and clear the emoji in BrickRow.tsx.

findings.title: pnpm audit:apca npm script is misconfigured and always fails
findings.detail: The script passes --target <dir>, but validate-apca.mjs expects a tokens.css file path as its positional arg; the first non-flag arg is treated as cssPath, so EISDIR is thrown and the script exits 2.
findings.evidence: pnpm audit:apca output: 'Cannot read tokens.css at /home/p31/production/portals/chat: EISDIR'. Direct run against tokens.css passes 72/72.
findings.recommendation: Change package.json audit:apca to point at the design-core tokens.css path, e.g. node .../validate-apca.mjs node_modules/@p31ca/design-core/src/css/tokens.css.

findings.title: e2e/sidebar.spec.ts dereferences nullable boundingBox() unguarded, and tsconfig excludes e2e
findings.detail: boundingBox() returns BoundingBox|null; the spec uses hb.x/hb.width, before.width/after.width, cb.y without null guards. The LSP reports 13 'possibly null' errors. They are not caught by typecheck because tsconfig include is only ['src'].
findings.evidence: tsconfig.json includes only src; sidebar.spec.ts:36,38,41,59 use nullable box values.
findings.recommendation: Guard with expect(hb).not.toBeNull() / non-null assertions, and add an e2e tsconfig (e.g. tsconfig.e2e.json) so playwright specs are typechecked in CI.

findings.detail: The audit file existed but contained no findings; this run populates it for the first time.
findings.evidence: File size 0 before write.
findings.recommendation: None — now populated.
